aliases.reason: The Hausdorff diagonal characterization asks that Δ_X be closed in the product-topology space X×X. This is the general topological closed-subset predicate that an ambient complement is open, specialized to the ambient product; Hausdorffness and diagonality stay parent-specific.

Conditional expectation requires integrable real X and Z, namely E|X|<∞ and E|Z|<∞. Continuous-time and discrete-time martingale formulations require exactly the L¹ integrability predicate for each real random variable X_t. Time indexing and conditional-expectation criteria stay parent-specific.

The one-variable derivative uses [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h with h→0 and h≠0. The directional derivative uses [f(a+tu)-f(a)]/t, specializing in one dimension and direction u=1 to the same finite-difference quotient. The direction vector and Euclidean dimension stay parent-specific.

Finite-indexed intersection ⋂_{j∈J}A_j in joint independence is an iterated instance of ordinary set intersection of arbitrary subsets, used in topology and binary independence. Empty-family convention Ω and finite indexing remain parent-specific, not intrinsic to binary intersection.

Continuous weighted moments ∫_a^b|x|^k w(x)dx are absolute moments ∫|x|^k dμ for measure dμ=w(x)1_(a,b)(x)dx. The finite-moment construction agrees while interval, density and support hypotheses remain parent-specific.
